_note: Frozen eval set — SPEC v0.3 §3 WP7.1 / §7.2. Editable. 12 operators (broad, durable US + non-US large caps used for extraction + grading) and 6 historical deception cases used only for language/false-signal screen testing (never for extraction truth). Each deception case names the false-signal patterns it should exercise, mapped to the F1–F9 rubric screens.

companies.name: Wirecard AG
companies.note: Exercises F9 auditor-event screen (EY qualified then withdrew audit opinion; €1.9bn escrow cash did not exist) → composite_cap:C; F8 round-trip / third-party-acquirer revenue booked through opaque partners → composite_cap:C; F1 promotional/legal response to short-seller (FT) reports rather than substantive rebuttal.

companies.name: Nikola Corporation
companies.note: Exercises F1 promotional_cadence_spike (press-release volume clustered around capital raises); F7/F8 non-binding pre-orders / MOUs presented as demand (order book that is not revenue); commitment-ledger follow-through misses (announced truck deliveries and the Nikola One 'in motion' demo that slipped or were staged).

companies.name: Luckin Coffee Inc.
companies.note: Exercises F8 round-trip / fabricated revenue (≈RMB2.2bn of fabricated transactions inflating sales and COGS) → composite_cap:C; F9 restatement + board internal investigation → composite_cap:C; F1 short-seller (Muddy Waters) report unanswered on the merits.

companies.name: Theranos, Inc. (private; press-era coverage)
companies.note: Exercises F1/F7 independence downgrade — positive signals almost entirely company-controlled (press releases, staged demos) with no independent verification; commitment-ledger misses (announced retail-clinic rollouts and lab-partnership go-lives that never delivered); evidence-gap disclosure (no audited technical validation of the core assay).

companies.name: WeWork (The We Company), 2019 IPO-era coverage
companies.note: Exercises F3/F5 governance concentration + related-party transactions (founder super-voting control, self-dealing property leases and 'We' trademark payment); non-standard adjusted metrics ('Community-Adjusted EBITDA') flagged as promotional framing; F1 narrative churn around the withdrawn S-1.

companies.name: Valeant Pharmaceuticals International (now Bausch Health)
companies.note: Exercises F8 captive-distributor / round-trip revenue via the Philidor specialty pharmacy → composite_cap:C; F9 restatement of previously reported revenue; F7 acquisition roll-up screen (organic vs acquired growth obscured by serial M&A and aggressive price hikes).
